newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar marches on the mark, bourses bouyant.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar marches on the mark, bourses bouyant.

text.p: The dollar romped ahead against the mark on Tuesday and European bourses, boosted by a bouyant Wall Street, also prospered, with British blue chips breaking records.
The dollar, which sneaked above the psychological 1.50 marks barrier in early European trade, continued to firm as the morning progressed, nudging the 1.5040 level.
Its rise followed comments on Monday by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that central bank governors in Basle had agreed a strong dollar was "in the interests of all".
This, together with the strong performance on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries, added up to a rising dollar.
Leading shares in London, Frankfurt and Paris all got a leg-up after the Dow Jones industrial average posted its biggest one-day gain in over a month to close 1.3 percent up.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index jumped 22.4 points to a record 3,933.2, surpassing its previous record of 3,922.1 set on August 28. On Monday it closed up 17.8 at 3,910.8 -- just short of its record closing high of 3,918.7, also set on August 28.
Traders said the market could hold on to its early gains through the rest of the session, as fears over U.S. interest prospects abated, boosting U.S. markets.
Some chart analysts said they believed the FTSE was set in a solid bullish pattern that will carry it to further record highs in coming sessions.

Yet Tuesday's gains were held in check by a lacklustre performance by government bonds, overshadowed by worries that Britain will cut interest rates further to stoke pre-election growth regardless of the inflation risk.

In Frankfurt, German shares started well ahead in electrnoic trading, cheered by Wall Street and the firmer dollar, and maintained their higher levels as bourse trade got underway. Dealers said sentiment was bullish and there was good potential for the market to go higher still.
The same motors, plus gains in the French franc, propelled Paris shares, which started firmer and quickly strengthened. The main CAC-40 index was more than one percentage point higher by 1030 GMT.
Stock and currency markets remained gripped by interest rate prospects following last Friday's U.S. jobs data showing lower unemployment and stronger earnings.

U.S. producer and consumer price data -- due Thursday and Friday -- will be scrutinised for fresh signs of inflation pressures. Many traders and investors are betting on a rise of 0.25 percentage point in U.S. interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
Opinions are mixed as to whether the central bank will decide this time to raise or leave interest rates unchanged, perhaps until after the November 5 presidential election.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5030 marks and 109.40 yen compared with late European levels on Monday of 1.4935 and 109.15.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
By 1000 GMT the Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had risen 22.4 points to 3,933.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 23.13 to 2,043.40.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 18.84 at 2,567.57.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at its lowest level since July 9 after a sell-off on Monday pushed prices below a key support level. Bullion fixed at $382.45 an ounce, compared with Monday's afternoon fix of $384.60 and close of $383.45. Silver was also easier at 507 cents.
